subject: Pilot burn-rate & breakeven scenarios — recap and next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Li <h.li@ledgerlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot burn-rate & breakeven scenarios — recap and next steps

Hannah — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and the concrete next steps so we have alignment.

Summary of pain points we heard
- Token burn for user-facing flows is the primary cost pressure (high qps on chat + embedding vector generation).
- 95/99p latency spikes on peak cause a bad UX — current goal is 99p < 350ms for model endpoints.
- Procurement/budget window is tight: pilot needs to land inside Q3 budget allocation.
- Security/compliance: team needs SOC2 evidence and a short security alignment call.

Goals you stated
- Proof-of-value pilot for core chat + classification pipeline over 3 months.
- Pilot cap: ~50k USD committed for infra/ops during pilot (you mentioned this number as the most realistic internal ceiling).
- Target throughput: ~3M infer calls/month at pilot scale (40–60k daily active calls).

Recommended cost levers (initial TCO view)
1) Model + precision: start with a smaller open model variant (7B/8B fp16) then test int8/4 quantization for production.
2) Batching: apply 16–64 token micro-batching for background embedding generation and 4–8 for chat where latency permits.
3) Prefix/KV caching: cache repeated system prompts and common prefixes to cut repeat decode cost.
4) Routing policy: route low-SLA traffic to cheaper model variants and reserve high-SLA to faster instances.

Attachments: tco-breakeven.xlsx (TCO workbook stub) — I attached a workbook with three scenarios (base, batching, aggressive-caching) to make ROI concrete. Also attached a 1-page summary (redwood-tco-summary.pdf).

Proposed next steps
- I will share the TCO workbook and a short baseline calculation by EOD (attached).
- Schedule a 60-min ops workshop to map call shapes and batching windows (Ben + Marissa + LedgerLane infra). Suggested windows: Tue/Thu next week, 9–11am PT.
- Security questionnaire: please send the initial set of questions (procurement@ledgerlane.com) and I’ll route to our security lead.

If you want, I can prepare three short ROI lines for the pilot (breakeven months at 3M calls) — I’ll send those in the next message so procurement can evaluate.

Thanks — looking forward to driving this forward.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hannah — thanks, helpful clarity. Quick ROI breakeven lines (assumptions are below). I put three scenarios into the attached workbook and included a short PDF you can share with procurement.

Assumptions (example basis)
- Avg tokens per call (decode + prompt): 220 tokens
- Baseline model cost (hosted fp16): $0.00018 per token
- Dedicated/quantized running cost (run-equivalent): $0.00008 per token
- Cache hit reduces token cost by 70% for the cached portion
- Batching effect: effective per-token cost reduction ~25% for batched flows (depends on batch size/latency)

Scenario math (3M calls/month):
1) Base (no batching, no caching)
- Monthly token footprint: 3,000,000 * 220 = 660M tokens
- Estimated hosted cost @ $0.00018 = $118,800 / month (~$356k over 3 months)

2) Batching-optimized (moderate batching + model selection)
- Assume 25% cost reduction via batching + model mix to cheaper variant = effective $0.000135 per token
- Monthly = 660M * $0.000135 = $89,100 / month (~$267k over 3 months)

3) Aggressive caching + quantization + routing
- Assume 40% of token volume can be cached at 70% discount and remaining quantized at $0.00008
- Effective blended monthly = ~$35,000 / month (~$105k over 3 months)

Breakeven vs 50k pilot commitment
- Under scenario 3, pilot spend (incl. runway + ops) would fall inside the 50k limit for an MVP with a tight feature set; full production at 3M calls would require a larger commitment or a phased rollout.
- We can engineer the pilot to validate cache-hit assumptions (which drive most of the gap).

Hosted vs Dedicated note
- Hosted is faster to start and will let us test assumptions; we can put hard spend caps and routing to limit cost exposure.
- Dedicated locks in lower unit costs but requires a larger up-front commit; likely outside the 50k range unless LedgerLane is comfortable with a longer-term reserved commitment.

Next steps I propose
- Ops workshop: collect call-shape + token histogram from you (you can drop to the Drive link) — Ben/Marissa will use that to tune batching/caching windows.
- Security: Hannah, once procurement sends the initial questionnaire to procurement@ledgerlane.com, I’ll route to our Security lead and attach SOC2 summary.
- Internal: I’ve looped Marissa to lead the pilot ops and Ben for technical sizing.

Proposed times for the workshop: Tue 5/18 10:00am PT or Thu 5/20 9:00am PT. Let me know which works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

—
